title: HA failover clears tenant-affinity header causing transient cross-organization API key access
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer-reported escalation: on Dedicated clusters with node-level HA failover we observed transient requests authenticated with a scoped API key being routed without the tenant-affinity header to a replacement node. The replacement node accepted the API key but failed to enforce the original org scope, allowing ephemeral cross-organization reads on a small percentage of requests. The issue affects Hosted fallback paths for Dedicated clusters and some Private deployments using the same proxy behavior.
impact_summary: Affects a subset of Hosted->Dedicated failover flows and Private deployments using node-level proxying. We have seen customer reports of 0.2–0.6% of requests during failover windows returning data from other tenant contexts. No evidence of persistent data exfiltration; access windows are short (seconds) and correlated with node failover and API key reuse patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a scoped tenant API key on a Dedicated cluster with at least 3 nodes behind the HA proxy.
2) Send a steady stream of low-latency requests that keep a persistent session open to node A (simulate customer traffic pattern).
3) Force node A to be removed (simulate OOM/crash) or trigger a manual failover via infra tooling.
4) Observe that some inflight requests are routed to node B without the X-Tenant-Affinity header set, and node B responds using a different tenant context for those requests.
5) Reproducible in stage with the same proxy config and session-affinity disabled or misapplied.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Rolling-restart proxy with patched config to preserve X-Tenant-Affinity for inflight handoffs (temporary hotfix rolled to impacted Dedicated clusters).
2) Applied strict validation on node B to reject requests where API key tenant doesn't match explicit org header and to return 401 instead of falling back.
3) Notified impacted customers and recommended temporary rate-limiting of cross-node session reuse while fix is deployed.
4) Added live query to detect mismatches and alert on any occurrences (dashboard link in attachments).
proposed_fix: 1) Runtime change: make tenant-affinity header atomic and persisted in the request context at the proxy level so it cannot be dropped during HA handoff.
2) Server-side hardening: enforce API key-org binding at token verification layer, independent of headers (defense-in-depth).
3) Add end-to-end tests in CI: simulate failover and assert no tenant-scoped API keys can access other tenant state.
4) Backfill: write a small migration script to scan recent access logs for anomalies and surface to security/CS teams for follow-up.
5) Release plan: patch in runtime-2.4.1, staged rollout to Dedicated, then to Private images.
qa_plan: 1) Create a stage Dedicated cluster with three nodes and instrument detailed request lineage IDs.
2) Run synthetic workload that triggers failover while validating tenant headers on each hop.
3) Run randomized chaos tests for 24h to validate no regression.
4) Add unit tests for header persistence and integration tests for token verification fallback.
rollout_strategy: 1) Canary to 1 Dedicated customer for 48h (opt-in), monitor alerts and logs.
2) Progressive roll to remaining Dedicated pools over 72h with auto-rollback on mismatch rate > 0.001%.
3) Private deployments: publish patch notes and provide assisted upgrade playbook to customers with on-prem packages.
4) Post-deploy verification sweep and customer confirmation for escalations.
